intent: A link to a page or section, either a direct top-level entry of a NavigationMenu or a row inside an open panel.
typical_uses: A row in a NavigationMenuContent panel, optionally with an icon and a description
A top-level entry that navigates directly, drawn like a trigger with navigationMenuTriggerStyle()

dont_use_when.situation: A link in running text or anywhere outside a NavigationMenu

instead.target: the consuming application's own link component (a plain anchor when it has none)
instead.note: This kit ships no Link component, and no kit component is a substitute for one: navigation belongs to the app's own router.

dont_use_when.situation: A step in the path to the current page

invariants.text: `active` sets `aria-current="page"` and `data-active` on the link; navigation-menu.module.css draws an active link with the secondary fill and a hairline, and keeps it under the pointer.
Clicking a link does not close the menu unless `closeOnClick` is given; moving focus out of the menu from a link closes it.
`size` sets the link's minimum height and block padding only; a link whose content wraps, such as one with a description, grows past it.
navigation-menu.module.css sizes every descendant `svg` of the link to the small icon size and keeps it from shrinking.

anti_patterns.dont: Style a direct top-level link by hand to match the triggers beside it
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `className={navigationMenuTriggerStyle()}`, the same class the triggers carry

a11y.by: the primitive's NavigationMenu.Link renders an `a` and sets aria-current="page" when active; navigation-menu.test.tsx asserts links are found by the link role and name, and that clicking one with closeOnClick removes the open content

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the link's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the link's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (active). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through navigation-menu.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A direct top-level link drawn like a trigger
The current page's link in a panel, compact, closing the menu on click
good.code:
<NavigationMenuContent>
  <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs/start" active size="compact" closeOnClick>
    Getting started
  </NavigationMenuLink>
</NavigationMenuContent>

bad.title: A link rendered outside any NavigationMenu
bad.why: The link reads the menu's state from the root's context, and the primitive throws when no NavigationMenu encloses it; use a plain link there instead.

companions.typed_by: a class-variance-authority recipe with no variants, returning a class string
companions.description: The class a NavigationMenuTrigger carries, for a direct top-level NavigationMenuLink that should look like a trigger without opening a panel.
